title: Hemp, Drug-Type Cannabis, and Botanical Versus Legal Categories
objective: Keep biological descriptors, production classes, chemotypes, and statutory definitions separate.

terms.definition: A legal or production term whose exact definition depends on jurisdiction and context.
A research and breeding descriptor for populations selected for intoxicating cannabinoid profiles; not a taxonomic rank.
A chemical phenotype defined by measured compounds or ratios.
A definition created by law for regulatory purposes.

coreScience: Hemp and drug-type cannabis belong to Cannabis sativa L. Their separation can reflect intended use, breeding history, architecture, photoperiod response, and cannabinoid profile, but no single visual trait reliably determines legal status. Fiber hemp, grain hemp, cannabinoid hemp, and drug-type flower are production categories with different target traits.

As of 2026-10-03, the current U.S. federal hemp definition in 7 U.S.C. §1639o still uses a delta-9 tetrahydrocannabinol concentration of not more than 0.3 percent on a dry-weight basis. Congress enacted an amended definition in 2025 that is scheduled to take effect on 2026-11-12 and will instead use total tetrahydrocannabinols, including THCA, together with additional exclusions. Because the controlling definition is time-sensitive, this encyclopedia records the effective date instead of presenting either version as a permanent plant-science boundary.

Chemotype classification is also not identical to legal status. A plant can have a CBD-dominant profile yet exceed a statutory THC limit. A young plant’s future chemistry cannot be established by appearance. A laboratory cannabinoid result alone is not a universal legal determination: jurisdiction, sampled plant part, sampling time, analytical method, measurement uncertainty, and administrative rules can all matter.
cultivationRelevance: Production advice must match the crop class. Results from grain or fiber cultivars may not transfer directly to dense indoor flower production, and vice versa.
For records, store intended use, measured chemotype, and legal classification in separate fields. This prevents one label from overwriting the others.

measureAndRecord.requirement: Fiber, grain, dual-purpose, cannabinoid hemp, drug-type flower, breeding, or research.
The actual production or research goal.
Laboratory result, sample stage, sample part, and date.
Country, state, province, tribe, or program.
Result under the cited current rule; do not infer from name or appearance.

misconceptions: Hemp is male cannabis: Hemp crops can be male, female, or monoecious depending on cultivar and purpose.

CBD-dominant automatically means legal hemp: Legal status depends on the applicable jurisdiction, sampling and testing rules, and administrative determination—not a product name or one chemistry label.
Plant height separates hemp and marijuana: Architecture is influenced by genetics, environment, density, and use, and is not a legal assay.
evidenceLimits: This is not legal advice. The current federal definition and its enacted future amendment were rechecked on 2026-10-03. The existing delta-9 definition remains controlling through 2026-11-11; the amended total-THC definition is scheduled to take effect 2026-11-12. State, Tribal, product, sampling, testing, controlled-substance, food/drug, and other requirements can differ and must be checked at the time of use.
